newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan players make shy SIMEX start, seen blooming.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan players make shy SIMEX start, seen blooming.

text.p: Taiwanese investors made a slow start on their first day of trading Taiwan-linked stock index futures on Singapore's futures exchange but interest is expected to pick up soon, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
They said Taiwanese participation was inhibited by players' unfamiliarity with trading the MSCI Taiwan index futures contracts listed on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX).
Eugene Chang, chairman of the Taipei Futures Association, told Reuters Financial Television individual Taiwanese investors needed more time to learn about trading futures contracts.

He said day traders and margin traders generated over a quarter of the daily turnover on the Taipei stock market. "They're familiar with the margin trading mechanism so these are the people we expect to be in the futures market way before the others," Chang said.
He said that on the institutional side, the Taiwan share market's bull run had heightened the need for a hedging instrument.

Taiwan's benchmark index stormed through the key 10,000 threshold earlier this week. The index shed 64.79 points to close at 10,001.56 on Friday in a muted response to the central bank's move to hike two key interest rates late on Thursday.
Chang said Taiwanese participants had probably accounted for about 500 of the total volume of over 3,200 lots in SIMEX Taiwan futures on Friday.

"SIMEX volumes increased about 30 percent, mostly contributed by Taiwan investors. It's not the big surge that we were expecting January 9 when both exchanges announced the launch of the futures contracts," he said.
SIMEX and the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) launched rival index futures pegged to proprietary Taiwan stock indices compiled by Morgan Stanley and Dow Jones, respectively, on January 9.
Taiwan regulators opposed the contracts, hoping index futures could be pioneered by the island's own futures exchange, now aiming to open in October.
To date, the SIMEX contract has fared better, with daily volumes averaging 1,000-2,000 lots against the CME contract, which often trades less than 100 lots.
SIMEX dealers said they had seen a noticeable increase in volumes on Friday, particularly in the first hour of trade.
The new lead August MSCI contract lost 13.8 points to end at 422.8 in line with a weaker finish on the Taipei share market.

"The bullish sign was that normally, for a new spot contract, we would only see small volumes of about 600 to 700 lots on the first few days," said Perry Gilbert, vice president of Refco Singapore Pte Ltd.
He estimated Taiwanese players accounted for about 700 lots of the total volume. "They were there in small sizes but they were there all day," he said.

Some dealers said turnover was dampened by the fact only two SIMEX clearing members in Taiwan -- UOB Bullion Futures Ltd and Fimat Futures Taiwan Branch -- were currently allowed to execute and clear orders from Taiwan brokerages.
They said the contract would fare still better once more SIMEX members were given permission to execute orders in Taiwan.
